sections.heading: How to Play Holy
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Holy"][color=paladin]Holy Paladin Rotation in Midnight[/color][/h2]
[pad]

Holy Paladin's rotation is fast paced and requires quick decision making. This can feel overwhelming at first, but the gameplay actually flows surprisingly smoothly once you get a feel for it. Hopefully, this page will help you get to that point. The core principles of playing Holy Paladin are summarized in these points:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_torch_thrown size=medium type=round color=c2 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c2]Spend and Generate Holy Power:[/color][/b] Your Holy Power spenders are some of your most efficient spells. The goal of the spec is to cast as many of these spenders as possible. Never cast a Holy Power generator if you are already at 5 Holy Power.

	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_ability_paladin_divinetoll size=medium type=round color=c2 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c2]Do not sit on your Cooldowns:[/color][/b] Strive to get as many uses of [spell=375576] and [spell=31884] as possible. If in doubt, use them. Saving them for a rainy day creates a rainy day. 
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_paladin_infusionoflight size=medium type=round color=c2 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c2]Do not waste Infusion of Light procs:[/color][/b] [spell=19750] with [spell=53576] is one of our strongest spells. It is important to spend the procs before casting more [spell=20473] which can generate new ones.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][wrapper width=800px][box border=true]If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

[center][cta-button=guide=32573 icon=spell_holy_holybolt]Holy Paladin Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center][/box][/wrapper][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=spell_holy_holybolt type=round size=medium inline=true color=c2][/icon] Best Holy Paladin Rotation[/h2]
For all forms of content, Holy Paladin follows a priority list of what spells to cast, rather than a set rotation. Below, we break down the priority lists for Healing and for Damage for Holy Paladins. We also include a few things to remember before pulling a boss or starting a key.

[pad]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Healing Priority" icon=spell_holy_searinglight]

sections.heading: Healing Priority
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Healing Priority" type=bar][icon name=spell_holy_searinglight color=c2 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] [color=c2] Best Holy Paladin Healing Rotation[/color][/h2]
[pad]

[wrapper width=850px]

[wrapper]
[center][box border=true]

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=c2][icon name=ability_paladin_beaconofinsight type=round size=small inline=true color=c2][/icon] Talent Choices[/color][/minor-heading]
[center]
[small][i]Talent options that are not included do not change the priority in any way. Hover over the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icons for additional information.[/i][/small]
[/center]
[center][wrapper]
[grid]
[display-option="Lightsmith" icon=inv_ability_lightsmithpaladin_holybulwark color=paladin]Lightsmith[/display-option]
[display-option="Virtue" icon=ability_paladin_beaconofinsight color=paladin checked]Beacon of Virtue[/display-option]
[display-option="AC" icon=ability_paladin_veneration color=paladin]Avenging Crusader[/display-option]
[/grid]
[/wrapper][/center]
[/box]
[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Healing Priority List[/color][/minor-heading]

[ol]
[li display-options="!Virtue"]Make sure [spell=53563] and [spell=156910] are active - [span class=tip tooltip=Faith][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li display-options="Virtue"]Cast [spell=200025] for AoE healing - [span class=tip tooltip=Virtue][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li]Spend Holy Power if on 5 Holy Power - [span class=tip tooltip=HolyPower][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li display-options="!Lightsmith"]Cast [spell=375576] on an Ally - [span class=tip tooltip=DT][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li display-options="Lightsmith"]Cast [spell=432459] or [spell=432472] - [span class=tip tooltip=HA][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] [/li]
[li]Spend [spell=53576] procs - [span class=tip tooltip=Infusion][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] [/li]
[li display-options="!Lightsmith"]Cast [spell=20473] on an Ally[/li]
[li display-options="AC"]During [spell=216331] cast [spell=1241288][/li]
[li]Spend Holy Power[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=82326] as needed and as mana allows - [span class=tip tooltip=Infusion][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li display-options="Lightsmith"]Cast [spell=20473] on an Ally[/li]
[li display-options="AC"]During [spell=216331] cast [spell=35395][/li]
[li display-options="Virtue"]During [spell=200025], cast [spell=19750][/li]
[li]Cast [spell=20271] [/li]
[li]Cast [spell=19750] [/li]
[/ol]
[/center][/wrapper]
[pad]
[hr]
[grid align=centered column-width=40% expand-columns=true width=80%]
   [section-header="Holy Power Spenders" width=50% collapse=true icon=inv_torch_thrown level=3 margin=half heading=none]
      [div][center][box level=2 margin=0 display='block']
         In both Mythic+ and Raids, [span display-options="Lightsmith"][spell=85673][/span][span display-options="!Lightsmith"][spell=156322][/span] is the best Holy Power spender. [spell=85222] should only be used if [span display-options="Lightsmith"][spell=85673][/span][span display-options="!Lightsmith"][spell=156322][/span] would overheal a lot.

[span display-options="!Lightsmith"]Do not worry about spreading the HoT from [spell=156322]. It does not heal enough to be important. Heal whoever needs it most, even if they already have the HoT.[/span]

Alternatively, if you do not need healing in the moment, [spell=53600] can be used. Besides dealing damage, it also returns a good bit of mana. As it doesn't have a mana cost either, it actually "saves" 2.4% of your mana per use compared to casting [span display-options="Lightsmith"][spell=85673][/span][span display-options="!Lightsmith"][spell=156322][/span] or [spell=85222].
      [/box][/center][/div]
   [/section-header]

   [section-header="Infusion of Light" width=50% collapse=true icon=ability_paladin_infusionoflight level=3 margin=half heading=none]
      [div][center][box level=2 margin=0 display='block']
         [spell=53576] procs are best spent on [spell=19750] if anyone needs the healing. [spell=20271] should be used if there is no good target for [spell=19750].

With [spell=387786] talented, you should ideally cast all your [spell=19750]s on players with any Beacon on them, unless you need to save someone else. Casting them on the target with [spell=1244878] heals the most, but it is also prone to overhealing, so generally just cast it on any Beaconed player that needs it.
      [/box][/center][/div]
   [/section-header]
[/grid][grid align=centered column-width=40% expand-columns=true width=80%]
   [section-header="Holy Light Usage" width=50% collapse=true icon=spell_holy_surgeoflight level=3 margin=half heading=none]
      [div][center][box level=2 margin=0 display='block']
 [spell=82326] is difficult to properly place in a Priority List. With it being our strongest spell, you could argue it should be above even spending Holy Power, but casting it even a couple of times much will decimate your mana. When playing with [spell=200025] you can barely afford to cast [spell=82326] at all.

With the Season 2 [url=spell=1296657]4-Set[/url], Holy Light always grants an [spell=53576] proc, so I recommend using it as a fallback spell when you have no [spell=53576], Holy Power, or [spell=20473] charge ready but you still need a lot of healing. 
If you have more mana to spare, you can prioritise it above [spell=20473] to guarantee Infusion procs when needed, but always spend your Holy Power and existing [spell=53576] procs first.

You generally manage your mana by casting more or fewer [spell=82326]. You want to have as many casts as possible over the course of a boss fight, without running out of mana before the boss dies.
      [/box][/center][/div]
   [/section-header]

   [section-header="Virtue Explained" width=50% collapse=true icon=ability_paladin_beaconofinsight level=3 margin=half heading=none]
      [div][center][box level=2 margin=0 display='block']
         [spell=200025] should be used close to on cooldown when you need any healing. With Beacon of Virtue in Raids, it is especially important that you use [spell=375576] and [spell=31821] (with [spell=1241542]) when Beacon of Virtue is running. In Mythic+, this is likely overkill so you might be better off separating your cooldowns from your Virtue windows. 

[spell=387786] should be used alongside Beacon of Virtue, so you should cast your Infused [spell=19750]s on targets with Beacon of Virtue or [spell=1244878]. Such Infused [spell=19750]s are your best spells during Beacon of Virtue.

It is also possible to pre-cast [spell=82326] into Beacon of Virtue. You simply spell queue Beacon of Virtue at the end of a Holy Light cast and it will transfer healing. This essentially gives you an extra spell's worth of healing transfer and guarantees you have an [spell=53576] proc for the Virtue window. While this combo is very powerful, it also costs an absurd amount of mana, so especially in raids, it is not recommended you do it often.
Note that this can be a bit finicky and often does [u]not[/u] work if you cast the [spell=82326] on yourself. 
      [/box][/center][/div]
   [/section-header]
[/grid][grid align=centered column-width=100% expand-columns=true width=100%]
   [center][section-header="Gameplay differences as Lightsmith" width=60% collapse=true icon=inv_ability_lightsmithpaladin_holybulwark level=3 margin=half heading=none]
      [div][center][box level=2 margin=0 display='block']
When playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-lightsmith] [color=c8]Lightsmith[/color] you gain a lot of free [spell=53576] procs from the [spell=432866] talent. Due to this you can rely a lot less on [spell=20473] to generate those procs, and this in turn saves a ton of mana which lets you cast more [spell=82326]s instead. With our Season 2 [url=https://www.wowhead.com/spell=1296657/paladin-holy-12-1-class-set-4pc]4-set Bonus[/url], each of these [spell=82326]s will also generate an [spell=53576] proc. So this is a self reinforcing loop, where you can end up almost not having to use [spell=20473] for healing at all.

This is reflected by [spell=20473]'s position in the Spell Priority above if you select [symbol=wow-hero-talent-lightsmith] [color=c8]Lightsmith[/color]. You will still use it for damage in m+ quite often to simply fill globals though.

[b]Holy Armaments:[/b]
[ul][li]It can be worth prioritizing [spell=432800] on squishy targets, but casting it on yourself will cause the extra Holy Bulwark from [spell=432802] to go on a tank. This does the most healing because tanks have more health than DPS players or healers.[/li]
[li][spell=432472] should just be cast on yourself to maximize healing. This will cause the extra Sacred Weapon to go on another random healer. If no other healer is available, such as in Mythic+, it will go on a DPS player. It will do the same damage/healing regardless of which DPS/healer it goes on.
With [spell=469701] talented, you can also use Sacred Weapon to create a mini Spirit Link between you and that target. This can be extremely strong for keeping that target, or yourself, alive through heavy damage, but can also be deadly if it occurs at a bad time.
[/li][/ul]
As for how you should prioritize these in your rotation, you generally just press them on cooldown when you need 3 Holy Power. Only use them with 2 or fewer Holy Power to avoid overcapping. 
Overwriting an existing [spell=432800] or [spell=432472] buff will immediately proc an [spell=53576], so keep that in mind and use it to your advantage.
      [/box][/center][/div]
   [/section-header]
 [/center][/grid]
[/wrapper]
[/tab]

[h2 toc="Single Target Priority" type=bar][icon name=spell_holy_innerfire color=c2 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] [color=c2] Best Holy Paladin DPS Rotation[/color][/h2]
[pad]

[wrapper width=850px] 
The main objective of the Damage priority is to generate and spend Holy Power. With the talent [spell=414113], [spell=20271] is your best generator to cast because each [spell=26573] from it stacks.
[wrapper]
[center][box border=true]


[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=c2][icon name=ability_paladin_beaconofinsight type=round size=small inline=true color=c2][/icon] Options[/color][/minor-heading]
[center][wrapper]
[grid]
[display-option="RJ" icon=ability_priest_holybolts01 color=paladin checked][spell=414113][/display-option]

[/grid]

[ol]
[li display-options="!RJ"]Keep [spell=26573] down[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=53600] if on 5 Holy Power[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=375576] on an Enemy [/li]
[li display-options="RJ"]Cast [spell=20271][/li]
[li]Cast [spell=20473] on an Enemy[/li]
[li display-options="!RJ"]Cast [spell=20271][/li]
[li]Spend Holy Power on [spell=53600][/li]
[li]Cast [spell=19750] for Holy Power[/li]
[/ol]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
When playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-lightsmith] [color=c8]Lightsmith[/color], to maximise damage, you need to use your [spell=384376] for damage as often as you can. The capstone talent [spell=433011] makes [spell=53600] deal much more damage than it normally does. It is especially powerful on large AoE pulls.
[/wrapper]
[/tab]
[tab name="Pre-Combat Checks" icon=inv_misc_paperbundle02a]

[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Checks[/h2]
Holy Paladin has a few things we need to remember to do before pulling a boss or starting a Mythic+ key.
[center][wrapper width=800px][box]
[ul]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Apply Beacon of Light and Beacon of Faith -[/b] [color=q0][spell=53563] and [spell=156910] make up a large portion of our healing, so you always need to make sure you have them out on players. Your best option is to put them on squishy ranged targets such as [color=mage]Mages[/color], [color=shaman]Shamans[/color], [color=hunter]Hunters[/color], or [color=druid]Boomkins[/color], but it can also be fine to put them on tank(s) if they need it.[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Enable Devotion Aura -[/b] [color=q0][spell=465] is the raid buff brought by Paladins. It is the only useful aura in PvE and should be enabled at all times. There is a macro to help you with this on the [url guide=3054][u]Macros page[/u][/url] of this guide [/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Apply Lightsmith Weapon Buffs -[/b] [color=q0]If you are playing Lightsmith, you need to remember to apply [spell=433568] or [spell=433583].[/color][/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[tab name="Common Mistakes" icon=petbattle_health-down]

sections.heading: Common Mistakes This is a list of the most common type of gameplay mistakes people make as Holy Paladin. Wasting Holy Power - Wasting Holy Power refers to casting Holy Power generators while on 5 Holy
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Common Mistakes[/h2]
[center][wrapper width=800px]
This is a list of the most common type of gameplay mistakes people make as Holy Paladin.
 [box]
[ul]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Wasting Holy Power -[/b] [color=q0] Wasting Holy Power refers to casting Holy Power generators while on 5 Holy Power already, and it is one of the most usual gameplay errors people make. Because Holy Power spenders are our most efficient spells, you want to cast as many of them as possible.

You can check how much Holy Power you are wasting by checking your logs. Click the resource tab and select Holy Power in the drop down. The Holy Power wasted in this screenshot, all comes from [spell=375576], which is completely fine to cast on 1 or 2 Holy Power. "Beacon of Light" is just how Holy Power from [spell=82326] and [spell=19750] gets logged.
[center][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/32957.png][/center][/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Focusing too much on Damage -[/b] [color=q0]While it is correct to optimise your damage output, it is easy to spend too many resources and cooldowns on it as a Holy Paladin. You are a healer first and foremost, and the fact is that the damage a healer does is inconsequential in most scenarios. Focus on learning to heal as best you can before trying to maximise your damage. 
Keeping your DPS players feeling safe, will also result in them doing more damage! [/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Casting Judgment too much -[/b] [color=q0]It is common for people to think they need to keep Judgment on cooldown, but when you need healing, [spell=53576] procs are best spent on Flash of Light. Spending them on Judgment is a significant healing loss if there are good targets to use Flash of Light on. Judgment is primarily used as a damage spell, which it is great for with the [spell=414113] talent. [/color][/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c2][icon name=spell_holy_avenginewrath type=round size=medium inline=true color=c2][/icon] Holy Paladin Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Holy Paladin has access to a few different cooldowns. The section below covers how they work and how to get the most out of each use.

[tabs uniform=true name="cds" iconborders=true]
[tab name="Divine Toll" icon=ability_bastion_paladin]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Divine Toll and Holy Prism[/color][/h3]
[spell=375576], or [spell=114165] if picked, should be used close to on cooldown when you won't be doing excessive overhealing with them. Due to them being such short cooldowns, you should not sit on them for too long.
[ul]
[li]Divine Toll should be used on an ally when you want it to heal, and on an enemy when you want to deal damage with it. To avoid excessive Holy Power wastage, you should only be using Divine Toll with 2 or fewer Holy Power.[/li]
[li]Holy Prism should usually be used on an enemy as this does the most healing, but if needed, it can also be cast on a specific friendly player. It should be used with 2 or fewer Holy Power.[/li]
[/ul]
As [symbol=wow-hero-talent-herald-of-the-sun] [color=c11]Herald of the Sun[/color], Divine Toll and Holy Prism lets you apply 2 [spell=431377]s. You can use [spell=156322] to apply them to specific targets, but when using [spell=85222] it will just apply them to a random target. Either option is fine and should not impact your choice of which Holy Power spender you are casting.

As [symbol=wow-hero-talent-lightsmith] [color=c8]Lightsmith[/color], they are replaced by [spell=432459] and [spell=432472].
[/tab]

[tab name="Avenging Wrath" icon=spell_holy_avenginewrath]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Avenging Wrath/Crusader[/color][/h3]
[spell=384376] is not a particularly powerful cooldown, but it does last a long time. With [spell=53376], it lasts 30 seconds. There is nothing special about it beyond the fact that it increases your healing, damage, and crit chance. It should mostly be used on cooldown when you need a healing boost, and you want to use it as often as possible. 

With the talent [spell=1242008], your next two (one with [spell=216331]) [spell=82326]s will be instant. You have 20 seconds to cast them, so don't just cast them right away if you don't need to, but obviously make sure to actually use them. With how powerful Holy Light is, this adds some much needed oomph to our main cooldown. Remember to also use the [spell=53576] procs each Holy Light grants.
[/tab]


[tab name="Aura Mastery" icon=spell_holy_auramastery]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Aura Mastery[/color][/h3]
In a coordinated raiding environment, the raid leader or healing officer will almost always designate a specific time to use [spell=31821]. If this is not the case, the best times to use this cooldown are when your group is going to be taking a lot of damage. 

As you should be using [spell=1241542], [spell=31821] becomes a very potent healing cooldown, and you actually want to use it when people are injured and not before. Although, if people are not topped off before damage is about to go out, it is fine to use it there. Remember that [spell=461244] makes overhealing not as detrimental.

When playing [spell=200025] in Raid, it is important that you don't cast [spell=31821] without [spell=200025] being active. In Mythic+, this will generally be overkill, so you should separate them to extend your cooldown coverage.
[/tab]

[tab name="Immunities and Externals" icon=spell_holy_divineshield]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Divine Shield, Blessing of Protection, and Sacrifice[/color][/h3]

[b][spell=642][/b] can be used in several different ways, the most obvious being to simply help yourself to stay alive in an emergency or when you make a mistake. Another very powerful use case in Mythic+ is to treat it as a \u201chealing\u201d cooldown. As there are only 5 players in a group, having one less person to heal essentially equates Divine Shield to a 20% overall damage reduction buff. Not having to worry about your own health can be extremely helpful for staying alive through heavy group-wide damage.
[hr]
[b][spell=1022][/b] makes the target immune to physical damage and effects, which means it can be used in the same ways as Divine Shield if the damage is physical. One of the main uses of this is to remove certain debuffs, like deadly bleeds or other physical debuffs from an ally. Keep in mind that the person you cast it on loses all aggro for the duration of the effect, so don't use it on the tank unless they ask for it.

The fact that Blessing of Protection causes aggro loss can also be used to your advantage, as using it on a DPS early in a pull will allow them to go all out on dealing damage without worrying about pulling aggro.
With [spell=387801], it also grants 15% damage reduction against magic damage, so it can also be used as a small external if needed.
[hr]
[b][spell=6940][/b] is our main external defensive. It has a relatively short cooldown so it should be used often. It will transfer the damage to you instead of the target, so it can be quite dangerous to use on tanks, but it is the best you can do if they need it. Just keep an eye on your own health. 

You [b]cannot [/b]use [spell=498] to reduce the damage you take from it, but you can use [spell=642] to completely immune the damage transferred. Using [spell=1022] on yourself also works if the damage the [spell=6940] target is taking is Physical.
With [spell=199422], it and Blessing of Protection will also be potent spot healing spells if needed in a crunch.
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Insights
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Insights" type=bar][color=c2][icon name=spell_paladin_lightofdawn type=round size=medium inline=true color=c2][/icon] Holy Paladin Advanced Insights[/color][/h2]
This section is for players who want to understand the intricate facets of how our more complex spells, talents, and various effects actually work. Most of these things are not important to know when it comes to playing the spec optimally but can be interesting and help you understand why we do things the way we do.

[tabs uniform=true name="insights" iconborders=true]
[tab name="Positioning"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Positioning of your character[/color][/h3]
Holy Paladin has in recent history been regarded by the community, and the game, as a melee healer. This meant that you were often not a viable target for many mechanics on raid bosses. This still continues to be the case, but Holy Paladin has lost nearly all reliance on melee-range positioning, other than [spell=53600] and [spell=35395] when specced into [spell=216331].

You can now do your complete healing rotation from ranged and are no longer bound by being in melee. This obviously gives you a lot of freedom when it comes to positioning, although it is still a benefit to be in melee due to [spell=183997] even if it is a small benefit. You will usually have your Beacons on ranged players, so they act as centers for your Mastery efficiency due to [spell=197446]. 
You should generally position yourself where you can heal the most players and where you feel safest. Your Mastery efficiency is a lower priority.
[/tab]

[tab name="Beacons"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Beacon Effects and Target Selection[/color][/h3]
Holy Paladin has several different Beacons; [spell=53563], [spell=156910], [spell=200025], and [spell=1244878]. These all work with any talent that otherwise only references "Beacon of Light" in their tooltip. 
[hr]
[b][color=paladin]Target Selection[/color][/b]
Your general targets for [spell=53563] and [spell=156910] should be ranged players, but they can also be fine to put on the tanks if they need it. Good targets are [color=mage]Mages[/color], [color=shaman]Shamans[/color], [color=hunter]Hunters[/color], or [color=druid]Boomkins[/color].

[spell=200025] should be cast on any target other than yourself that needs healing. You shouldn't cast any Beacon  on yourself because [spell=447985] prevents Beacons from healing yourself as long as there is any absorb shield remaining.

You generally want to avoid healing targets with Beacon of Light, Faith, or Virtue directly because Beacons only transfers from healing done to other targets. Obviously, if you think they need a direct heal to stay alive, you should heal them directly.

Casting spells on the [spell=1244878] target is fine though, because that target takes 20% increased healing which makes up for the lost transfer, and when running [spell=387786] you should be casting all your [spell=19750]s on players with a Beacon on them.
[hr]
[b][color=paladin]Transfer Rates[/color][/b]
At baseline, [spell=53563] transfers 10% of healing done. With [spell=387781], it becomes 15%.
When specced into [spell=156910], both it and your normal Beacon of Light get reduced by 30%. This makes both Beacons transfer at 10.5%, for a combined transfer value of 21%.
[spell=200025] transfers at 10% per target baseline, or 15% with Commanding Light.
[spell=1244878] also transfers 10% baseline, or 15% with Commanding Light. With the other Apex Talents, [spell=1245367], it transfers 25%.

Only "direct" spells transfers healing to Beacons. This was done to stop an issue that caused lag for the whole group in large raid sizes. [spell=216331], [spell=85222], and [spell=114165] (when used on an enemy) are the only non-direct spells that transfer to Beacons, but Light of Dawn and Holy Prism transfer at a 50% reduced rate. 
[spell=633], HoTs, and healing from things like trinkets do not transfer to Beacons.
[/tab]


[tab name="Mana Management"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Mana Management[/color][/h3]
If you have excess mana you need to spend, [spell=82326] is a great spell to use more frequently.

If you are running out of mana too quickly, you should be casting fewer Holy Lights. 
Beyond that, you can use [spell=53600] or use [spell=20473] offensively more often.  Shield of the Righteous returns 1.8% mana while costing no mana itself, so you save 2.4% mana per cast by using it in place of a healing Holy Power spender. Holy Shock returns half its mana cost when used for damage, which saves you ~1% mana per cast compared to using it for healing.

Both these options are significant healing losses so it might be difficult to find time to do it, especially on hard raid bosses, but if a boss has downtime where healing is not needed, it is recommended that you do it.
[/tab]

[tab name="Mastery"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Mastery: Lightbringer[/color][/h3]
Our Mastery causes us to heal more the closer we are to the player being healed. Due to [spell=197446], all our Beacons targets also counts as centers for our Mastery efficiency, and it will be based on whichever is closer. Our Mastery efficiency is 100% within 10 yards of yourself or your Beaconed targets, and drops off linearly to 0% at 40 yards, which is the maximum range of your spells.

This means that if you have 40% Mastery, you will heal 40% more to people within 10 yards, 20% more to players at 25 yards, and 0% more to players at 40 yards.
[pad]
[center][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/32080.png][/center]
[/tab]

[tab name="Miscellaneous"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Miscellaneous[/color][/h3]


[b][color=paladin][spell=231644][/color][/b]
If Greater Judgment is active on a mob that then does an AoE attack that hits multiple people, Greater Judgment will just absorb damage done to the first player hit in the combat log. If there is leftover absorption on the Greater Judgment, it will simply overflow to the next player hit, and so on. It will not absorb the stated amount on all players hit. 
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=6940][/color][/b]
The damage transferred to you from having Blessing of Sacrifice on someone else is not reduced by any kind of damage reduction on yourself. This means you cannot use [spell=498] to reduce the damage you take from it. Other damage reductions on the targeted player will reduce the overall damage they take and the subsequent damage transferred to you.

You can use [spell=642] to completely immune the damage transferred. Using [spell=1022] on yourself will only prevent you from taking damage if the Sacrifice target is taking Physical damage.

Blessing of Sacrifice cannot kill you. It will fall off once you hit 20% health. If used on one single giant hit that would bring you below 20%, it will absorb 30% of the damage the target takes, but only transfer enough to bring you to 20% before immediately falling off.
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=1241714][/color][/b]
Seraphic Barrier reduces the healing your Holy Power spenders do by 15%, but instead applies an absorb shield to the target equal to the healing reduced. Due to the lost transfer to Beacons, this talent is a significant healing loss when you are not overhealing with your Holy Power spenders. 
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=461287][/color][/b]
Liberation simply causes Holy Power spenders to deal 12% of their raw healing as damage to a random target. It uses the same wording ("converts") as Seraphic Barrier, but does not actually reduce the healing of your Holy Power spenders.
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=414113][/color][/b]
There is no limit to how many [spell=26573] can be active at once from Righteous Judgment. They all have independent durations, and they will all deal damage and heal (with [spell=377128]) independently from each other.
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=447985][/color][/b]
Light of the Martyr only ever applies the healing absorb to yourself. The healing absorb cannot be healed off by any Beacon effect. This is to prevent people from putting a Beacon on themself to try and negate the negative effects.

When going above the 70% health threshold with [spell=448040], you always start with 1 stack of Bestow Light, meaning the Light of the Martyr healing increase starts at 25% instead of 20%.
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=406101][/color][/b]
Faith's Armor only ever applies the armor bonus to yourself regardless of who the [spell=85673] or [spell=156322] was cast on.
[hr]
[b][color=paladin][spell=431474][/color][/b]
[spell=20473]s from Second Sunrise can proc [spell=53576], meaning as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-herald-of-the-sun] [color=c11]Herald of the Sun[/color], each Holy Shock cast has a roughly 19% chance to proc Infusions instead of the normal 10%.
[spell=85222]s from Second Sunrise can proc [spell=431413], and Light of Dawns cast by consuming [spell=1241358] also procs Second Sunrise.

[/tab]




[/tabs]
 

[hr]
Our Holy Paladin guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Holy Paladin guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page.
[pad]


[pad]

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false]Feedback[/h2]

Thanks for reading our class guides! If you have any feedback, feel free to leave a comment in the section below, and we will reply as quickly as possible. If you'd like to talk with any of our writers directly, you can do so by joining our [url=http://discord.gg/wowhead]Discord server[/url] and finding them there!

[pad][br][pad]

[tooltip name=NotesHighlight][color=q]Notes will appear in a tooltip window like this.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=HolyPower][color=q]Read Notes below.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=DT][color=q]Only with 2 or fewer Holy Power. 
Always consume [spell=223817] procs first. 
Make sure you cast it on an ally.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=HA][color=q]Only with 2 or fewer Holy Power. 
Can simply cast them on yourself. I explain target selection in the Lightsmith section below.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=HL][color=q]If needed and if your mana allows.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Infusion][color=q]Read Notes below.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Faith][color=q]Keep them on two DPS players. Only put them on on the tank(s) if they genuinely need it.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=Virtue][color=q]In Mythic+, I recommend casting it on yourself to avoid as many issues with the 30 yard radius as possible.
In Raids, cast it on anyone but yourself.[/color][/tooltip]
